newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank says housing affordability grows.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank says housing affordability grows.

text.p: Housing in most parts of Canada is now the most affordable it has been in more than decade, the Royal Bank of Canada said on Monday.
Canada's largest bank said homes in every province except British Columbia reached their most affordable level since it began measuring the cost of home ownership in 1985.
The bank measures affordability using an index that measures the proportion of pre-tax income taken up by home ownership costs. The index reached a new record low in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The bank credited mortgage rates which are at their lowest in more than 30 years for the increase in housing affordability. At the end of 1996 the five year mortgage rate in Canada was 6.95%.

Atlantic Canada and Alberta remained the most affordable areas in the country in the last quarter of 1996 as interest rates declined further, house prices remained low and household incomes increased moderately.
Royal Bank forecast that while a six-year-long improvement in housing affordability will come to an end in 1997, a significant deterioration is not likely.
